In mathematics, '''Mahler's 3/2 problem''' concerns the existence of "{{math|''Z''}}-numbers".

A '''{{math|''Z''}}-number''' is a positive real number {{math|''x''}} such that the  [[fractional part]]s of

:<math> x \left(\frac 3 2\right)^ n  </math>

are less than {{math|1/2}} for all positive integers {{math|''n''}}.  [[Kurt Mahler]] conjectured in 1968 that there are no {{math|''Z''}}-numbers <ref>{{cite journal | first1=Kurt | last1=Mahler | title=An unsolved problem on the powers of 3/2 | journal=The Journal of the Australian Mathematical Society | volume=VIII | number=2 | year=1968 | pages=313–321 | doi=10.1017/S1446788700005371 | zbl=0155.09501 | issn=1446-7887 | doi-access=free }}</ref>.

More generally, for a real number {{math|''α''}}, define {{math|Ω(''α'')}} as

:<math>\Omega(\alpha) = \inf_{\theta>0}\left({ \limsup_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left\lbrace{\theta\alpha^n}\right\rbrace - \liminf_{n \rightarrow \infty} \left\lbrace{\theta\alpha^n}\right\rbrace }\right). </math>

Mahler's conjecture would follow if {{math|Ω(3/2)}} exceeds {{math|1/2}}.  Flatto, [[Jeffrey C. Lagarias|Lagarias]], and Pollington showed<ref>{{cite journal | first1=Leopold | last1=Flatto | first2=Jeffrey C. | last2=Lagarias | author2-link=Jeffrey C. Lagarias | first3=Andrew D. | last3=Pollington | title=On the range of fractional parts of&nbsp;''&zeta;''&nbsp;{&nbsp;(''p''/''q'')<sup>''n''</sup>&nbsp;} | journal=[[Acta Arithmetica]] | volume=LXX | number=2 | year=1995 | pages=125–147 | doi=10.4064/aa-70-2-125-147 | zbl=0821.11038 | issn=0065-1036 | doi-access=free }}</ref> that

:<math>\Omega\left(\frac p q\right) > \frac 1 p </math>

for rational&nbsp;{{math|''p''/''q'' > 1}} in lowest terms.
